name: Total Knee Replacement
description: Complete replacement of the knee joint with artificial components
insights: Total knee replacement costs range from $20,000 to $70,000 depending on facility.
Ambulatory surgery centers can save you 40-60% compared to hospital ORs.
Implant choice significantly affects price - ask about different options.
Many patients qualify for bundled payment programs that include rehab.

name: Partial Knee Replacement
description: Replacement of only the damaged portion of the knee joint
insights: Partial replacements cost 20-30% less than total knee replacements.
Recovery time is typically faster than total knee replacement.
Not all patients are candidates - depends on extent of arthritis.
Outpatient partial replacements are becoming increasingly common.

name: Knee Arthroscopy
description: Minimally invasive surgery to examine or treat knee joint
insights: Arthroscopy costs can range from $5,000 to $15,000+ depending on location.
Outpatient surgery centers offer significant savings over hospital ORs.
Physical therapy costs post-surgery should be factored into total expense.
Some surgeons offer cash-pay packages that bundle all related fees.

name: Meniscus Repair
description: Arthroscopic surgery to repair torn meniscus cartilage
insights: Meniscus repair preserves the cartilage and is preferred over removal when possible.
Recovery takes 3-6 months compared to 4-6 weeks for meniscus removal.
Younger, active patients typically benefit most from repair vs. removal.
Some facilities offer package pricing that includes post-op physical therapy.

name: Meniscus Removal (Meniscectomy)
description: Arthroscopic surgery to remove damaged meniscus cartilage
insights: Meniscectomy is less expensive than meniscus repair.
Recovery is faster - most patients walk within days.
Long-term, removal may increase risk of arthritis compared to repair.
Often performed as outpatient surgery with same-day discharge.

name: ACL Reconstruction
description: Surgical reconstruction of torn anterior cruciate ligament
insights: ACL reconstruction costs range from $15,000 to $50,000.
Graft choice (autograft vs. allograft) affects both cost and recovery.
Physical therapy is essential - budget 6-9 months of rehab costs.
Many sports medicine centers specialize in ACL surgery at competitive rates.

name: PCL Reconstruction
description: Surgical reconstruction of torn posterior cruciate ligament
insights: PCL injuries are less common than ACL tears.
Surgery is typically only needed for complete tears or combined injuries.
Recovery timeline is similar to ACL reconstruction (6-9 months).
Specialized knee surgeons may have better outcomes for this procedure.

name: Knee Manipulation Under Anesthesia
description: Procedure to break up scar tissue and improve knee motion
insights: Often performed when knee becomes stiff after surgery or injury.
Less expensive than revision surgery if performed early.
Typically done as outpatient procedure with quick recovery.
Success rates are highest when performed within 3 months of stiffness onset.

name: MRI Knee w/o Dye
description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the knee without contrast
insights: Knee MRIs are essential for diagnosing ligament and cartilage injuries.
Freestanding imaging centers charge 40-60% less than hospitals.
Some insurers require trying physical therapy before approving knee MRIs.
Open MRI machines may cost less but provide lower image quality.

name: MRI Knee w/ Dye
description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the knee with contrast
insights: Contrast MRI may be needed for complex cases or surgical planning.
Adds $100-300 to the base MRI cost for the contrast agent.
Provides better visualization of certain injuries and conditions.
Not always necessary - ask your doctor if contrast is truly needed.

name: Knee X-Ray (3+ Views)
description: X-ray examination of the knee from multiple angles
insights: X-rays are the most affordable knee imaging option.
Best for detecting fractures, arthritis, and bone alignment issues.
Cannot show soft tissue injuries like meniscus or ligament tears.
Often the first imaging step before MRI is ordered.

name: Knee Joint Injection
description: Injection of medication into the knee joint
insights: Can include cortisone, hyaluronic acid, or PRP injections.
Office-based injections cost significantly less than hospital settings.
Cortisone provides quick relief but effects may be temporary.
Some insurers limit the number of injections covered per year.

name: MRI Lumbar Spine w/o Dye
description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the lower back without contrast
insights: MRI prices can vary by 300-500% between hospitals in the same area.
Outpatient imaging centers typically charge 40-60% less than hospital-based facilities.
Cash prices are often lower than insurance rates if you haven't met your deductible.
Ask about "self-pay" discounts - many facilities offer 20-40% off for upfront payment.
